issues.description: The solution implementation of set_pixel treats the label display_start as memory content (uses [display_start]) instead of as the base address. The problem statement and the template define display_start as the start address of the framebuffer (a label/address). Using [display_start] dereferences uninitialized bss memory and yields an incorrect base pointer, causing the pixel write to target a wrong location. This is a structural bug in the provided solution and would confuse students trying to follow the example.
issues.suggestedFix: In set_pixel, treat display_start as an address, not as dereferenced memory. For example, compute the pixel offset in eax then add the label address (add eax, display_start) or load the base with mov esi, display_start and add esi, eax, then store with mov [esi], ecx. Do not use add eax, [display_start]. Ensure registers are preserved as required (push/pop) when needed.
